accounting.charge: every byte actually read is charged to the global, library and window counters, on success and on every failure path (partial, oversized, mismatched), and each retry attempt is charged again
accounting.index_download: charged to the library and global counters
accounting.window_cap_source: window counter is the transport's, not only count_window's successful return

completion.complete: exactly the 330 expected identities present and all 330 usable; nothing else is called complete
completion.expected_identities: 330 = 10 libraries x 33 windows (11 amplicons + 22 comparison); built from controls.json, must be unique
completion.no_promotion: a lower or missing count is never replaced, rescaled or promoted
completion.partial_data: all 330 identities present but at least one unusable (failed rows are kept, excluded from summaries, never imputed)
completion.stopped_on_bound: a runtime/request/byte bound ended the run; rows completed so far kept, missing identities listed
completion.stopped_on_error: an unexpected exception ended the run; rows kept, exception type recorded

frozen_before: any target-window read; trigger: admission review infra-to-regulatory-transport-review.md of packet b59f3501 / source 6048ee7
independent_crosscheck: fixtures indexed and queried by htslib (pysam 0.24.1, samtools/htslib 1.24) are committed as bytes with htslib's own counts; the same reader must reproduce them; the real 0dpa1 index is checked against htslib's contig list; pysam is a test-time tool only, not a packet dependency
supersedes: only the transport, accounting and completion-status clauses of protocol.json (sha256 7a2ec7be…); windows, controls, count rule, summary rule and scientific questions are unchanged and protocol.json is not edited

transport.bounded_read: read at most expected_length+1 bytes; one extra byte means oversized -> refused; response closed on every path
transport.order: open the response, check HTTP status and Content-Range first; for any status other than 206 close the response and read zero body bytes (unsupported_range)
transport.preflight: before a request is sent, refuse it if its expected length would take the global, per-library or per-window total over its cap
